title: Slot0 price manipulation + zero-slippage liquidity removal enables direct WETH extraction from AerodromeAMO
chain_description: Phase 1 (FL-003): attacker manipulates Aerodrome Slipstream slot0 before strategist rebalance, causing mintForStrategy to mint excess OETHb, leaving the pool OETHb-heavy. Phase 2 (FL-006): attacker sandwiches the subsequent _removeLiquidity call (amount0Min=amount1Min=0), which costs less capital because Phase 1 already skewed the pool toward OETHb. Together these extract real WETH from the vault without any privileged access.
root_cause: getPoolX96Price() reads clPool.slot0() directly (no TWAP), enabling front-running of _addLiquidity to over-mint OETHb. _removeLiquidity passes amount0Min=amount1Min=0, enabling MEV extraction via sandwich. _solvencyAssert is blind to the imbalance because _updateUnderlyingAssets uses a fixed parity constant (sqrtRatioX96TickClosestToParity), not spot price — excess OETHb in the position is counted as WETH-equivalent.
impact: An MEV actor front-runs the strategist's rebalance to mint excess OETHb (pool becomes OETHb-heavy), then sandwiches the next _removeLiquidity call (zero slippage) to receive zero WETH. Phase 1 reduces the capital cost of Phase 2. Combined they produce a net WETH shortfall in vault withdrawal queue fulfillment.
fix: Phase 1: replace clPool.slot0() with a TWAP (Aerodrome observe() over 30 min) in getPoolX96Price(). Phase 2: compute expected token amounts via principal() or getAmountsForLiquidity at current spot, apply governance-configured slippage tolerance as amount0Min/amount1Min.
